previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and history of chronic cyclic nausea with dry heaves and poor solid-food tolerance was admitted to the surgical service after planned Interventional Radiology gastrostomy tube placement to transition from TPN to enteral nutrition for protein-calorie malnutrition. Post-procedure she tolerated clear liquids, then after 24 hours started tube feeds that were advanced to goal and cycled for home use, with improvement in nausea and tolerance of a regular diet as able. Pain was limited to mild tube-site discomfort controlled with oral medication; she remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without infectious complications. She was discharged home with services on goal tube feeds and free-water flushes, with PICC removed and instructions for tube-site care and return precautions.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was admitted to the ___ surgical service from the 
ED following 1 week of left upper quadrant abdominal pain 
exacerbated by eating and tube feeding administration.  She was 
subsequently placed on bowel rest, given intravenous fluids/ 
banana bag, pain medication, and pantoprazole.  Imaging 
including a chest x-ray and KUB were negative for free 
intraperitoneal air.  Additionally, Gastroview had been 
administered via the G-tube to assess for blockage/ tube 
positioning; no extrastravsation was noted and contrast was seen 
throughout the small bowel.  

On HD#2, the patient underwent an EGD, where a single 10 mm 
ulcer was found in the gastro-jejunal anastomosis.  The 
jejuno-jejunal anastomosis appeared normal and the 
pancreatico-biliary limb mucosa was normal through the duodenal 
bulb. Post-procedure, the patient was maintained on intravenous 
pantoprazole with oral sucralfate.  Tube feedings were resumed, 
however, patient reported increased pain at her cycled rate of 
110 mL/hr; feeds were subsequently changed to a continuous 
regimen at 55/mL/hr.  The patient reported improved, but 
persistent pain at this rate, therefore, her regimen was further 
adjusted to a concentrated formula at 30 mL/hr with ongoing 
pain.  Additionally, her diet was progressed to a Bariatric 
stage 5; the patient was able to consume moderate amounts of po 
intake, however, reported pain with eating.  Due to pain, tube 
feedings were discontinued on HD7 and TPN was initiated via PICC 
(placed HD7) for nutrition support.  An abdominal CT scan was 
subsequently obtained without evidence of obstruction or 
gastrogastric fistula.  Also, on HD7, a pustule was noted in the 
supraumbilical area, which was opened and cultured for MRSA. The 
patient remained afebrile without evidence of spread of 
infection.

Repositioning of the G-tube was considered, however, 
Interventional Radiology felt this was not possible due to small 
size of the gastric remnant.  Conversion to a GJ tube was 
considered, however, the patient declined. Given no obstruction, 
tube feedings were retrialed on HD12; TPN was discontinued at 
this time and the PICC was removed on HD13.  The patient 
complained of increased pain with resumed tube feedings, worse 
at night/ improved during the day.  Her feeding regimen was 
again adjusted to Peptamen Bariatric, which was well tolerated.  
Therefore, her cycled rate of 60 mL/hr was trialed and also well 
tolerated.  

She was subsequently discharged to home on ___.  At the 
time of discharge, the patient was afebrile with stable vital 
signs.  She continued to tolerate moderate amounts of oral 
intake without increase in pain and tube feedings were continued 
on a cycled regimen.  She will take liquid Protonix BID as 
recommended by Gastroenterology and sucralfate orally and via 
Gtube.  She will follow-up with Dr. ___ in 1 week and Dr. 
___ in 3 weeks.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with left-sided abdominal pain 
exacerbated by oral intake and tube feedings.  An EGD was 
performed and revealed a gastrojejunal anastamotic ulceration.  
You were treated with intravenous pantoprazole and sucralfate 
orally and via your G-tube and will be discharged with a 
prescription for liquid pantoprazole and sucralfate.  
Additionally, your tube feeding regimen was adjusted to provide 
adequate nutrition in a smaller volume of a 'pre-digested' 
formula for improved tolerance. 

You are now preparing for discharge to home with the following 
additional instructions:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.
Please resume all regular home medications , unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.
Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.
Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.
You must not use NSAIDS (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) 
Examples are Ibuprofen, Motrin, Aleve, Nuprin and Naproxen. 
These agents will cause bleeding and ulcers in your digestive 
system

Basic Gastrostomy Care:
Dressing
The area around the tube may be washed with mild soap and water.
When there is no drainage around the tube, the dressing may be 
omitted.

Prior to Feeding
The tube should be aspirated with a 60ml syringe prior to 
feeding to check for residual food.
If more that 50 ml is aspirated, stop the feeding and notify the 
physician who has ordered your formula.

Please note, your Nortriptyline dosage has been increased from 
25 to 50 mg at bedtime at the recommendation of the pain 
service.  A new prescription for 50 mg tablets has been provided 
to you; please discontinue taking your 25 mg tablets. 
Please notify your prescribing provider, primary care provider 
and therapist of this dosage adjustment immediately.

with p.o. intolerance.

lungs to pubic symphysis after administration of oral contrast via mouth as
well as via the gastrojejunostomy tube as well as the nonionic intravenous
contrast.  Multiplanar reformatted images were prepared and reviewed.

FINDINGS:

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV AND ORAL CONTRAST:

Visualized lung bases demonstrate bibasilar linear atelectasis.

Tiny calcific focus is noted at the upper portion of the spleen (2:2),
suggestive of prior granulomatous disease.  Otherwise, the spleen is within
normal limits.

The patient is status post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with a gastrostomy tube in
place. The gastric remnant appears within normal limits and contains no oral
contrast. Contrast flows freely throughout the remainder of the bowel and into
the colon with no evidence of obstruction.  The liver, gallbladder, pancreas,
bilateral adrenal glands are within normal limits.  Again noted is a wedge
hypodensity in the inferior pole of the left kidney suggestive of prior
infarction (2:27). Otherwise, bilateral kidneys are within normal limits. 
There is no free fluid or free air in the abdomen.  There is no mesenteric or
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber and

lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions
suspicious for malignancy.
